name: Gatorade
note: Sports drink brand; Lidl-Trek partner from the 2026 kit (jersey front per the launch coverage). Gatorade is a division of PepsiCo, a listed US company whose largest holders are Vanguard (10.1%) and BlackRock (8.2%) per its 2026 proxy. ON HOLD: the ownership chain is state-free, but major-NGO investigations have tied PepsiCo to child and forced labour findings within the last 20 years - Amnesty International's 2016 'The Great Palm Oil Scandal' (amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2016/11/palm-oil-global-brands-profiting-from-child-and-forced-labour/) names PepsiCo among companies whose palm oil was produced with children working in hazardous conditions, and the 2016-2017 RAN/ILRF/OPPUK investigations (ran.org press releases) found child labour and worker exploitation at Indofood plantations, Indofood being PepsiCo's joint-venture partner producing PepsiCo snacks in Indonesia. Whether these pass METHOD.md's company test is for a maintainer.
